svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
Juice Shop · 20.1.1 · 7 components · 19 data flows · 6 trust boundaries · 67 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-02; tb-2 External → C-03; tb-10 C-02 → External; tb-12 C-05 → External
Trust boundary crossing: tb-8 C-02 → C-07; tb-9 C-02 → C-06

df-002: POST /rest/user/login — credential submission (step 1 of login) (HTTPS) df-003: POST /rest/2fa/verify — TOTP code submission (step 2 of login) (HTTPS) df-002 authentication: unauthenticated login endpoint; no token required to present credentials; evidence: routes/login.ts:34 df-002 access group: Credentials (2FA if enrolled); sequence; step 1 df-003 authentication: temporary token issued after successful password step, before full JWT is granted; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:17, server.ts:458 df-003 access group: Credentials (2FA if enrolled); sequence; step 2

df-006: Authenticated REST API request with RS256 JWT bearer token (HTTPS) df-007: Unauthenticated public API request (registration, browsing, feedback, file upload) (HTTPS) df-006 authentication: RS256 JWT in Authorization header; 6-hour expiry; signed with hardcoded RSA private key; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:16, lib/insecurity.ts:54 df-006 access group: API access (authenticated or public); alternatives; step n/a df-007 authentication: no authentication required; endpoint class includes user registration, product catalog, feedback submission, and file upload; evidence: server.ts:182, routes/fileUpload.ts:19 df-007 access group: API access (authenticated or public); alternatives; step n/a

df-008: POST / — cookie-authenticated data erasure request (HTTPS) df-008 authentication: session cookie checked in routes/dataErasure.ts handler; separate from JWT bearer authentication used by the API; evidence: routes/dataErasure.ts:76

df-009: Socket.IO WebSocket connection for challenge events and score broadcasts (WebSocket) df-009 authentication: No authentication check; confirmed by T-041 (evidence-verified); evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23

df-010: Sequelize ORM SQL queries (raw SQL with interpolated inputs on login path) (SQL) df-010 authentication: Embedded SQLite engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-011: marsdb document queries ($where built by string concatenation on product reviews) (MarsDB) df-011 authentication: Embedded MarsDB engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9, data/mongodb.ts:10
df-012: Server-side fetch to user-controlled URL for profile image upload (SSRF candidate) (HTTP)
df-013: Ethereum JSON-RPC call to Alchemy Sepolia for NFT minting and wallet verification (HTTPS)
df-014: HTTP POST webhook notification on challenge completion (HTTP)
df-015: HTTP GET startup health probe and API call to Ollama/OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint via /rest/chat (HTTP)

df-016: GET /metrics — unauthenticated Prometheus metrics endpoint (HTTP) df-016 authentication: management endpoint publicly reachable with no authentication check; authn_signal absent on production route R-108; evidence: server.ts:676, routes/metrics.ts:73

df-017: HTTP requests to /rest/web3/* endpoints for key submission, NFT verification, and wallet exploit (HTTPS) df-017 authentication: Web3 endpoints have missing_auth_suspect=true in route projection; no authentication check located in handlers; evidence: routes/checkKeys.ts:1, server.ts:641
Internet Attacker → C-03 · Authentication & Session Surface: scenario 1, 2, 3, 4; its findings also affect C-02 · Express REST API Server
Internet Attacker → C-02 · Express REST API Server: scenario 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7; its findings also affect C-05 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface
Internet Attacker → C-05 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface: scenario 2
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6, 7

Dynamic code evaluation — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:61, routes/captcha.ts:22

Further capabilities: XML parsing — evidence: lib/xml.ts:38; Server-side templates — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:87 (reported finding); LLM calls — evidence: lib/startup/validatePreconditions.ts:236

C-07 · SQLite Relational Store: User Credentials
C-07 · SQLite Relational Store: User Personal Data
C-07 · SQLite Relational Store: Payment Card Data
C-07 · SQLite Relational Store: Order and Basket Data
End user accessing Juice Shop via web browser. May be anonymous or authenticated; when self-registration is open, anonymous reaches authenticated in seconds.
Google OAuth 2.0 authorization server. The Angular SPA performs an implicit-flow redirect (response_type=token) without a state parameter.
Arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS URL submitted by an authenticated user for profile image upload. The server fetches this URL server-side, enabling SSRF.
Alchemy Ethereum Sepolia RPC endpoint used by NFT minting and wallet exploit-address challenge handlers.

g.title: Ollama or OpenAI-compatible LLM inference endpoint. Validated at startup via GET to the /models path; used by the /rest/chat route handler.
Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.

Google OAuth 2.0 df-004: OAuth implicit-flow authorization redirect to Google (no state parameter) (HTTPS); OAuth 2.0 implicit flow; SPA redirects browser to Google authorization endpoint with response_type=token; missing state parameter (CSRF risk) df-005: OAuth implicit-flow access token returned in URL fragment to /oauth callback (HTTPS); access token in URL fragment delivered by Google OAuth authorization server; implicit flow (no PKCE) df-018: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
URL fetch = requests a URL that runtime input selects or influences
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.
The recipient performs no authentication check on this connection.
The recipient checks the token supplied with the request.
A session cookie identifies the caller.
Delegated access; only the evidenced protocol step is covered.
temporary token issued after successful password step, before full
Authentication could not be determined from the code.
Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
Method properties, not proof of a secure implementation.
